newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM testifies in Hungary punch case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM testifies in Hungary punch case.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz gave testimony to prosecutors on Thursday in a case against assailants who allegedly punched him in the face in a Budapest hotel last year, Anatolian news agency said.
It said Yilmaz was called to the state security court to give testimony against four Turkish men accused of taking part in an attack on Yilmaz in a hotel lobby in the Hungarian capital last November.
Yilmaz, then opposition leader, said at the time that he had received threats for attempting to reveal evidence linking state officials with organised crime as part of a security scandal.

He did not report the incident to Hungarian police but complained to legal authorities when he returned to Turkey after a short stay in Budapest. Turkish courts have the power to deal with alleged crimes abroad if all involved are Turkish citizens.
Yilmaz required minor surgery and had to wear a large white plaster on his nose for some time after the attack.
He became prime minister last month at the head of a secularist coalition that replaced the Islamist-led government of Necmettin Erbakan.
